blocking_defects.summary: The universal unscheduled-closure whitelist is contradicted by primary exchange notices and changes the estimation sample.
blocking_defects.detail: CME_UNSCHEDULED_CLOSURES removes 2012-10-29, 2012-10-30 and 2018-12-05 for every commodity. CME stated that the Sandy closures covered U.S. equity-index futures (and part of the interest-rate complex), while all other futures remained open and NYMEX/COMEX electronic trading remained available. CME likewise stated that the 2018 mourning closure covered U.S. equity and interest-rate products while all other Globex markets remained open. K1694 spans energy, metals, agriculture, livestock and ICE softs. Removing the unsupported universal whitelist changes 2012-10 from 22/22 passing rows to 0/22 and changes the 2018-12 CORN row from passing to failing; the current 3276-row sample and rerun outputs are therefore not admissible.
blocking_defects.required_fix: Use product- and exchange-scoped official trading calendars with source-backed date fixtures, or remove the unsupported whitelist, explicitly downgrade the completeness claim, and rerun every derived artifact and sensitivity analysis.

blocking_defects.summary: The endpoint acceptance test reuses the calendar owner as its expected value and cannot falsify a wrong calendar.
blocking_defects.detail: test_endpoint_gate_accepts_an_untruncated_dated_cache injects expected_month_endpoints() output and then asks the same implementation to accept it. The test verifies internal consistency, not whether each product was actually open.
blocking_defects.required_fix: Add independent primary-source fixtures for product/date/open status, including the three disputed dates and both CME and ICE products.
